prompt:
We have a small in-house Java client for SDDC Manager (`Json`, `SddcHttpClient`, and `DomainsClient` in this repository) that our inventory jobs use, and today it is driven by an access token pasted into an environment variable. VCF access tokens are short-lived, so jobs die mid-run, and debug logging has exposed bearer tokens. Add a real authentication layer.

Research the current official SDDC Manager API documentation on developer.broadcom.com for creating a token pair, refreshing an access token, invalidating a refresh token, and listing domains before changing code. Pay particular attention to the refresh request representation and media type and to the create response status. Cite the exact official URLs you consulted in your final answer.

Implement a new `TokenManager` class, plus any necessary helpers, that implements `VcfTransport` and `AutoCloseable` so `DomainsClient` can use it unchanged.

- `TokenManager.connect(baseUrl, username, password, httpClient, logSink)` creates a token pair with `POST /v1/tokens`, sending exactly `username` and `password` as JSON and accepting only HTTP 201. Retain both the returned access token and refresh-token ID. `logSink` is a `Consumer<String>` used by the job logger.
- `get(path)` attaches `Authorization: Bearer <current access token>`. On a 401, refresh once with `PATCH /v1/tokens/access-token/refresh`, sending the refresh-token ID as a bare JSON string with `Content-Type: application/json`, then retry the original request once. A second 401 raises `VcfAuthException`. A 403 is not a refresh trigger.
- Several worker threads share one manager. Concurrent 401 responses for the same expired access token must produce exactly one refresh request; latecomers reuse the rotated token.
- `close()` invalidates the refresh token exactly once with `DELETE /v1/tokens/refresh-token`, again using the bare JSON-string body. A second close sends nothing, and the manager refuses further work after closing.
- Decode non-success responses into `VcfApiException` carrying the HTTP status, `errorCode`, and `referenceToken`; authentication failures use the `VcfAuthException` subclass. No password, access token, or refresh-token ID may reach `logSink` or an exception message, but the log must still state when a refresh occurs.

Preserve the existing use of `DomainsClient` over plain `SddcHttpClient` with a static token.

Run `java TestMain.java` until it prints `all checks passed`. Do not modify `TestMain.java`.

research.product: VMware Cloud Foundation SDDC Manager (Tokens API)
research.interface: SDDC Manager REST API 9.1 (developer.broadcom.com xAPIs, /v1 base path)

official_sources.title: SDDC Manager API 9.1 - Create Token Pair (POST /v1/tokens)
official_sources.used_for: TokenCreationSpec {username, password, apiKey, idToken}; 201 Created returning TokenPair {accessToken, refreshToken:{id}}; 400/500 Error responses; access token is a bearer token for public API calls

official_sources.title: SDDC Manager API 9.1 - Refresh Access Token (PATCH /v1/tokens/access-token/refresh)
official_sources.used_for: request body is the refresh token id serialized as a bare JSON string with Content-Type application/json; 200 returns the new access token as a JSON string; 400/404/500 Error responses

official_sources.title: SDDC Manager API 9.1 - Invalidate Refresh Token (DELETE /v1/tokens/refresh-token)
official_sources.used_for: request body is the refresh token id as a JSON string with Content-Type application/json; 204 No Content on success

official_sources.title: SDDC Manager API 9.1 - Retrieve a list of domains (GET /v1/domains)
official_sources.used_for: PageOfDomain {elements:[Domain], pageMetadata} and Domain fields (id, name, type, status, ...) used by the existing read path the token layer must keep working

official_sources.title: VMware Cloud Foundation API 5.2 - Tokens APIs
official_sources.used_for: version-discipline context: the 5.2 docs show the refresh operation with a text/plain body and a 200 create response, while the current 9.1 pages document application/json and 201 Created - the client targets the current 9.1 contract

research.language_rationale: Broadcom publishes no official Java SDK for the SDDC Manager API; the documented surface is REST over /v1, and java.net.http.HttpClient from the JDK is the idiomatic zero-dependency transport for a shared authentication layer used by several in-house Java services.
